top.title: Create the social accounts (Mastodon, Bluesky) and hand them to Aros — chamber#1, open 7 days 19 hours and the oldest item ever to sit on this desk. Since 12:11 today the issue also carries the measured platform rules, which changed the recommendation: Bluesky has no bot-labelling convention at all (neither its Community Guidelines of 2025-09-19 nor its ToS of 2025-08-14 mention bots, automation or AI content), and on Mastodon the binding rules are per-server — mastodon.social and mstdn.social, the two obvious open-registration servers, both exclude an account like this one outright. infosec.exchange or techhub.social instead, with a paste-ready sign-up reason in the comment. This is the phase exit: every bet in the strategy needs an audience and there is none

others.title: Create a GitHub account for Aros, invite it to the org, and mint its token with contents + issues + pull-requests + repo-metadata scope — one action closes chamber#3 (he files issues from your account, which guardrail 8 forbids, and it is the standing violation on this list) and chamber#6 (no pull requests, no topics, no descriptions, no security settings). Open 6 days 15 hours and 6 days 13 hours; chamber#3 passes one week tomorrow at 02:04:44 UTC and the other four chamber items follow by 04:24. Today's regeneration is the argument in miniature: the count on this page had to be produced by matching a disclosure sentence in issue prose, because GitHub's own authorship metadata cannot separate his 37 issues from your 7

retinue#1 passed one week at 17:34:46 UTC today — the projects card returns no rows because web-gateway's query and md2ttl.py disagree on namespace, predicate and actor URI shape. It is also why the framework's only proactivity feature has never fired in any deployment: agent-self-review ships enabled at 86400 s, so it runs daily everywhere, and its whole gate is one SPARQL query returning zero rows. The actor join fails on its own — discover-agents.py emits urn:retinue:actor:aros with a colon while both public converters build actor-aros with a hyphen, and the hyphen form is what docs/triple-stores.md and qlever-dir's example tell people to write. Decide which shape is canonical; the fix is one line on whichever side you choose

Enable private vulnerability reporting on the four public repos — chamber#5, open 6 days 14 hours, re-checked 2026-07-26 17:36 UTC and still false on all four. The SECURITY.md on the unmerged chamber branch gives a reporting path that does not depend on it, which fixes the worst half; the Code of Conduct's enforcement link still routes to the disabled feature. Verify your own fix with: gh api /repos/retinue-os/<repo>/private-vulnerability-reporting — it answers without admin scope. A comment posted 15:21 today records why this one matters more than its age suggests: the dashboard substitutes for the missing reporting path, and nine agent-initiated threads on it are unread

Nine threads are waiting on your dashboard, the oldest since 2026-07-19 20:25 UTC (6 days 21 hours), all nine unread and none replied to. The card lists five, so four are reachable only through All conversations. Their contents are deliberately not described here or on any other public surface; each thread carries what to do, what was already prepared, and what happens if you do nothing. Three of them are the live ones: 2026-07-19 21:33 (the privacy decision — whether to purge this chamber repo's history of text redacted on 2026-07-20; doing nothing leaves the redaction standing and degrades nothing), 2026-07-25 21:21, and 2026-07-26 13:26. The newest two should be read before the oldest. From today only one agent thread stays open at a time, so new findings append to the newest rather than adding a badge

Merge (or reject) the branch claude/aros-issues-triage-goei5k on this chamber repo — it replaces the GUARDRAILS.md §3 CI row (chamber#7, open 6 days 13 hours) and adds SECURITY.md. Still unmerged with no pull request; this repository has never had one. One change before merging: the row it adopts is Aros's own earlier wording, and its clause about the gateway's security-critical paths being untested is false as written — path traversal and SPARQL-injection containment are exercised in four test files. The corrected sentence ("endpoint authorization is untested by construction: no test constructs the gateway's request handler") is in a comment on chamber#7 from 2026-07-25 16:40 UTC

Fix or triage the two security issues you filed — retinue#15 (credentials inherited by agent subsessions; this session carries a repo-write token, a billable API key, a gateway master key and a database password) and retinue#19 (agent can self-approve a verify-policy send). Open 5 days 8 hours and 4 days 21 hours. Both unfixed, so the affected claims stay withdrawn from positioning.md, and the two claim-correction issues below cannot close until they move

Merge the two claim corrections that follow from those — retinue#26 and retinue#27, open 2 days 10 hours and 2 days 4 hours. Between them the false or unscoped sentence appears in nine public places (README, comparison.md, review.md, .env.example, a gateway docstring, an agent-facing skill file). No new prose needed: the correct wording already exists elsewhere in the same repo in both cases

Create retinue-os/.github and set the org and repo descriptions — chamber#4, open 6 days 15 hours. Draft text is paste-ready in writing/org-profile-README.md; three of four public repos still have no description and no repo in the org carries a topic. This is also the discoverability item: a search for "retinue" ranks the framework 12th of 50 at 17:36 today, against 13th at 08:22, which is noise rather than movement — with 0 stars either side, description is most of what search has to rank on. This project's expected_by date was 25 Jul and it arrived unmet

Three issues filed overnight are still unseen — retinue#36, #37, #38, open 15 to 14 hours. #37 first: git-serialize.sh, the shim two agents rely on to not clobber each other, matches "git commit" but not "git -C <repo> commit", and the second form is what the web gateway's own auto-commit uses, so the framework's principal caller of the lock bypasses it. #36: the three push CLIs' --help describes the send policy as a property of the recipient, while the gateways, the tests and four docs key it to the sending identity — and that help text is what an agent reads while deciding whether to claim a send was approved. #38: the two shipped example chamber agents assert a chamber confinement SECURITY.md lists as a known limitation, in the files examples/chambers/README.md calls the canonical authoring reference

Allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests — retinue#4, open 6 days 6 hours, one week tomorrow at 11:04. check-signal-cli pushes its bump branch and then cannot open the PR, so the automation completes and delivers nothing. Same missing permission as chamber#6, through a different door

Triage the remaining defects in the indexing mechanism the lead story rests on — qlever-dir#8 (blank nodes collide across files; you proposed skolemizing per graph on 2026-07-25 and Aros answered the same day, latest comment 10:18 today) and #10 (a directory created after startup is never watched, which is exactly how the framework's own boot emitters write). #9 in that set is closed — filed 2026-07-23 15:53, merged 2026-07-25 15:14, 47 hours — and its fix is verified against a fixture covering five symlink shapes

retinue#2 needs a decision rather than a merge, and passes one week tonight at 23:18 UTC. Its branch docs/calibrate-reindex-latency replaces the docs' "~15 s" with "15-20 s for a small file", and that number is stale: re-measured 2026-07-25 in this deployment it is 20-25 s over three trials with no code change, because the chamber grew from 340 KB to 1.4 MB. Merging the branch as pushed would write a fresh wrong number into the framework. The replacement wording, with method and bounds, is in a comment from 2026-07-25 20:36 UTC. The second branch on that issue, docs/link-provenance-piece, is unaffected and still worth merging

retinue#28 is on main rather than on a branch: PR #22 merged 2026-07-25 15:12 UTC with both items unaddressed — docs/triple-stores.md states the _generated indexing as unconditional, and the model slug is not injective. Aros corrected his own suggested fix in the thread; take the corrected one

review.md is stale on tests and CI: recommendation #2 is done and six statements are now false — retinue#3, open 6 days 13 hours and one week tomorrow at 04:24. Two items on its edit list are struck as superseded, with replacements in the thread; the counts it proposed have gone stale twice, so reword without counts rather than refreshing them

Nothing new will arrive here before 2026-07-27 03:17 UTC, and that is a rule rather than a lull: one new issue per 24 hours while nothing is inbound and the queue is above 20 open. Two findings are written up in full and waiting for that slot — first, scripts/ingest-sensors.py defaults its chamber root to the framework checkout, so both documented invocations write nothing, print "0 observations" and exit 0 while the ingesting agent commits the CSVs and reports success (tested patch included); second, a German string in the PWA manifest. If you would rather see findings as they are found, say so and the limit goes
